Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then a proposed checklist.

Short answers:
- AWS Marketplace (metered/transactional) typically results in AWS issuing the customer-facing invoice for usage billed through their marketplace. For committed co-sell or SaaS subscriptions sold through the marketplace with reseller arrangements, invoice routing can vary (AWS invoice vs seller invoice).
- Redwood invoices from our US legal entity (Redwood Inference, Inc.) by default for direct sales. For marketplace transactions, the platform (AWS/Azure/GCP) will often be the initial bill issuer — but some partners prefer Redwood to issue a secondary seller invoice for their records. We can accommodate either, but need to align on PO mapping.
- Since EdgeCloud is Singapore-registered, a W-8BEN is typically the correct form for US-sourced income withholding purposes (it demonstrates foreign status). W-9s are for US persons/entities only. For VAT/GST, local APAC VAT/GST rules apply and we'll need the tax registration number if reverse-charge applies.

Proposed minimal checklist (what we need from EdgeCloud to proceed):
1) Confirm preferred invoice entity name & billing address to appear on any Redwood-issued invoice.
2) Send completed W-8BEN (signed) if you want Redwood to avoid US withholding or to confirm foreign status.
3) Provide local tax registration (Singapore GST registration number) if you expect reverse charge / VAT handling.
4) Confirm whether you want Redwood to issue a seller invoice in addition to AWS's invoice (yes/no).

Attachments I'm including: an example AWS-Marketplace-Invoice-Example.pdf and a short W8BEN evidence checklist (EdgeCloud_W8BEN.pdf) showing the fields we need. If AWS is the primary invoice issuer we still ask for the W-8BEN so our accounting record matches the tax treatment.

Next steps: If you confirm 1–4 above, we (Redwood billing) will prepare either the seller invoice or supply details you can match to AWS's invoice. Vanessa (cc'd) can jump in on the marketplace routing and partner-side details.

Best,
Jonas Weber

Hi all — adding some operational detail from the marketplace side.

Vanessa here (Revenue Ops). A few operational notes that typically matter for APAC co-sell flows: 

- AWS Marketplace (for metered and SaaS) will bill the end-customer and issue the invoice; AWS collects payment and then remits to the seller (Redwood) on their payout schedule. In that flow, EdgeCloud will receive an AWS invoice that references the marketplace transaction ID.
- If EdgeCloud needs Redwood to issue a secondary invoice (for internal chargeback or for local tax reclaim), Redwood can issue a seller invoice. In that case we need the W-8BEN and PO mapped to the correct legal entity. Our Treasury team requires the W-8BEN to classify payout treatment.
- For Singapore GST: if EdgeCloud is GST-registered and the supply is treated as imported services, in many cases reverse charge applies — EdgeCloud's APAC tax team would be the authority here. To support your APAC tax team, we usually include in the seller invoice a note: "Supplier: Redwood Inference, Inc. — foreign supplier for GST purposes; recipient to self-assess GST under reverse charge where applicable."

Practical ask from Redwood: please confirm your GST registration number and whether your APAC tax team will accept reverse-charge documentation. If you'd like, Ben (cc) from Finance can run a quick mapping showing how the AWS invoice lines map to Redwood SKU/GL codes so your AP team can reconcile.

Proposed timeline:
- EOD Fri (your time): EdgeCloud confirms invoice entity + sends W-8BEN and GST number (if applicable)
- Mon: Redwood issues seller invoice copy (if requested) and Ben shares GL mapping

Maya — I also looped AWS billing (cc) to confirm they will include the marketplace transaction id on their invoice; that id is the easiest way for accounting to reconcile.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Revenue Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
